newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart has higher earnings, sees more gains.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart has higher earnings, sees more gains.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc., the world's largest retail chain, reported higher fourth quarter earnings Tuesday and said it racked up its 26th consecutive year of record sales and profits.
David Glass, president and chief executive officer, said he expected the current fiscal year to show higher earnings and improvement in its stock price.
Glass made the comment as the retailer reported record profits of $3.056 billion, or $1.33 a share, for the year ended Jan. 31 on record sales of $104.9 billion.

Wal-Mart charmed investors Tuesday with its strong fourth quarter earnings and bullish forecasts for 1997, sending its stock higher in active trading. It was up $1.75 to $26.375 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Naming Wal-Mart among retailers that are strong now and are going to do much better in the future, Otto Grote, an analyst with Derby Securities, said, "Consumer confidence is coming back and retailers are becoming a strong play."
Last year the company reported profits of $2.74 billion, or $1.19 a share, on sales of $93.63 billion.

For the quarter ended Jan. 31, Wal-Mart earned $1.095 billion, or 48 cents a share, up from $942 million, or 41 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose to $30.84 billion from $27.55 billion a year earlier.
All operating divisions reported an increase in the sales growth at stores open at least a year and improved profits over the prior year, Glass said.
The company's international division recorded an operating profit of $65 million for the most recent quarter, compared with a loss of $13 million a year earlier.
For the year, the division recorded an operating profit of $24 million, compared with a year-earlier loss of $16 million.
For the fourth quarter, the company's Wal-Mart division, including Supercenters, had an operating profit of $1.888 billion vs. $1.651 billion for the same period last year.
Fiscal year operating profit for the division was $5.548 billion, a rise of 11 percent over the $5.020 billion reported last year.

Wal-Mart's Sam's division recorded operating profit for the quarter of $274 million compared with $231 million for the same prior year quarter. Sam's operating profit for year ended Jan. 31, was $864 million, an increase of 8 percent over the $800 million reported in the prior fiscal year.

Separately, Little Rock, Ark.-based Dillard Department Stores Inc. reported higher earnings for the final quarter and said its board approved a Class A common share repurchase programme of up to $300 million.
The company said it would make the purchases from time to time on the open market.
Dillard earned $111.1 million, or 98 cents a share, for the fourth quarter, up from $29.1 million, or 26 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose to $1.94 billion from $1.92 billion.
For the year, Dillard earned $238.6 million, or $2.09 a share, up from $167.2 million, or $1.48 a share, a year earlier.
Sales increased to $6.23 billion from $5.92 billion in the year earlier period.
Dillard stock was up $1.75 to $29.875, also on the NYSE.
